intended_object: For a normal subgroup object i : H → G that is the kernel of a group-object morphism q : G → Q (i.e. H is the pullback of q along the unit η[Q]), the canonical natural map of group presheaves G(X)/i(H(X)) → Q(X), [g] ↦ q ∘ g, induced by q (the pointwise first-isomorphism-theorem map). Inferred from the docstring, the module doc and the subsequent lemmas (factorization through quotientMk, pointwise injectivity).
explanation: The body applies the file's general `quotientLift` to the map on points induced by q, which is componentwise `QuotientGroup.lift` of postcomposition with q. The side condition (the range of i on X-points lies in the kernel of q on X-points) comes from `monoidHom_range_eq_ker_of_isPullback`, using only its ≤ direction. So each component sends [g] to q ∘ g, as intended. Only the identity i ≫ q = 1 is needed to build the map, so the pullback hypothesis is stronger than necessary. It matches the docstring's "kernel subgroup object", and the next lemma, `yonedaQuotientMap_app_injective`, uses the full kernel condition to prove injectivity. The setting, an arbitrary cartesian monoidal category, is the natural one for group objects, and the general version for group-valued functors is already in this file. I found no Mathlib definition of this map.
